title: Bird Banter #2: The Eagle Who Waited

story.want: to be fed for ever without ever having to hunt
story.lesson: Those who only ever take will one day find nobody left to give.
reversals: The dry season makes every fish cost his mother more.
The family meets in secret and he blames the squirrels.
The family leaves, and even the squirrels stop laughing.
story.open_thread: Who left the fish on the ledge?

music_prompt: a slow, wry instrumental bed with a heavy, patient pulse that warms into tenderness, no drums

characters.eagle: Orin: a big golden-brown eagle with a pale crest, heavy-lidded sleepy eyes, a round plump chest and gleaming talons that have never touched anything
characters.mother: Sela: Orin's mother, a lean dark-brown eagle with sharp amber eyes, a scarred left wing and a permanently tired stare
characters.brother: Kest: Orin's younger brother, a small quick eagle with a white-tipped tail and an eager, hopeful face
characters.squirrels: Three small red squirrels called Pip, Nip and Tuck, bushy tails, round gossipy eyes, always chewing acorns, perched together on an oak branch
characters.witness: Witness: a small grey marmot sitting upright on a rock, perfectly still, with a blank, unmoved face
characters.human: Sam: a plain white round-headed stick figure in a grey hoodie and black trousers, thin dark outline, big worried eyes.
characters.colleague: Jo: a plain white round-headed stick figure in a navy sweater with a lanyard, thin dark outline, tired eyes.

scenes.narration: Orin the eagle ate three hundred and twelve fish. He had caught none.
scenes.image_prompt: Orin sprawls on a high cliff ledge like a bloated emperor, eyes half-shut, belly round, a monstrous tower of clean fish skeletons stacked beside his nest as tall as he is. Below, in a great oak, three squirrels cling to a branch with tiny paws held up, tallying on their claws. The marmot sits on a rock behind, blank.
scenes.image_prompt_b: The skeleton tower wobbles and a single bone slides off the top. Orin opens one lazy eye and lowers his chin, offended, while the three squirrels below gasp in unison.

scenes.narration: Down in the oak, three squirrels kept count.
scenes.image_prompt: Close on the three squirrels in the oak, mouths full of acorn, each holding up a different number of claws with deadly seriousness, heads swiveling to stare up at Orin on the cliff above. Orin, small and distant, is clearly aware of them and pretends not to be.
scenes.image_prompt_b: All three squirrels burst into silent, shaking laughter at once, acorns tumbling from their cheeks, tails flicking, while one slaps the branch.

scenes.narration: Hunting, Orin explained, was for birds with nothing better to do.
scenes.image_prompt: Orin, chin raised to the sky, wing pressed theatrically to his chest, delivers his verdict like a king addressing parliament. Far below, the squirrels roll helplessly on their branch, one hanging upside-down by his tail, doubled over.

scenes.narration: Sela caught the fish. Orin ate the fish. The squirrels objected.
scenes.image_prompt: Sela lands on the ledge with a silver fish in her talons, wings still spread, breathing hard, and lays it before Orin, who is already leaning toward it with eyes shut. Below, the squirrels wave tiny arms in protest, one holding a rolled leaf like an official petition.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Orin's beak is closing on the fish, eyes still shut and utterly content, while Sela steps back, wings drooping, with a flat stare. A squirrel throws his own tail up in despair.

popups.prompt: a tiny rolled leaf scroll tied with grass

scenes.narration: Little Kest brought lunch. He was still learning to fly.
scenes.image_prompt: Kest crash-lands onto the ledge in an explosion of loose feathers, a large fish clutched in both talons, wings tangled, tail in the air. Orin lifts one eyebrow and extends a wing to accept the fish without getting up. In the oak below, the squirrels grab each other, mouths wide in horror.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Kest pulls himself upright, feathers sticking out everywhere, pushing the fish toward Orin with a proud, breathless grin. Orin is already chewing. One squirrel faints backward off the branch.

scenes.narration: Then the dry season came. Now, the fish grew scarce.
scenes.image_prompt: The river valley below is cracked and shrunken, a thin brown trickle where a wide silver river used to run, white fish bones scattered on dry stones. Orin on the ledge looks politely curious about the mud. The marmot, in the foreground, watches without a flicker.

scenes.narration: Sela flew farther each day. Her wing began to tremble.
scenes.image_prompt: Sela flies low and alone across a pale scorched wasteland, scarred wing beating with effort, the horizon empty. Her shadow is long behind her. A single feather drifts off her wing into the heat haze.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Sela is closer to the camera now, beak open, eyes narrowed in pain, the scarred wing visibly shaking mid-beat.

scenes.narration: She laid the fish before him and swayed. He didn't look up.
scenes.image_prompt: Sela, hollow-eyed and shaking, sets a small fish in front of Orin and sways on her talons, one wing drooping to the ground. Orin, beak open, stares off to one side at nothing. Far below in the oak the three squirrels have gone completely still, one frozen with an acorn halfway to his mouth, staring up at her.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Sela's knees give a little as she steadies herself on the stone. Orin's beak closes on the fish while his eyes stay on the horizon. The squirrel's acorn slips from his paws and falls without a sound.

scenes.narration: That night, the family met without him.
scenes.image_prompt: By moonlight on a lower branch, Sela and Kest sit close with beaks nearly touching, a heavy moon behind them. The three squirrels have crept silent along the oak branch, trying to look asleep, ears twisted toward the meeting. In the foreground the marmot watches. High above, Orin's silhouette snores on the ledge.

scenes.narration: Orin heard it all. He blamed the squirrels.
scenes.image_prompt: Orin's silhouette is awake on the ledge, one eye wide in the dark and glaring down at the oak with absolute certainty, a self-satisfied narrow look on his beak. In the oak, the squirrels pretend to be asleep, all three with one eye cracked open.

scenes.narration: People build nests too. Usually with a sofa.
scenes.image_prompt: Sam, a plain stick figure in a grey hoodie, sprawls on a living-room sofa surrounded by cushions, a laptop closed on his knees and a TV remote in hand, perfectly comfortable.

scenes.narration: Sam never finished a report. Jo always did.
scenes.image_prompt: In a dim open-plan office, Jo, a stick figure in a navy sweater, types furiously at a desk piled with two people's work, while Sam, behind her, leans back with his hands behind his head. A clock on the wall shows late evening.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Jo's fingers blur over the keyboard, shoulders hunched, while Sam checks his phone and smiles.

scenes.narration: Jo stayed late. Sam called it teamwork.
scenes.image_prompt: A dark office, one desk lamp glowing over Jo, who rubs her eyes, an empty coffee cup at her elbow. Sam stands at her shoulder wearing his coat, giving a thumbs-up.

scenes.narration: Then Jo changed jobs. Monday's report stayed blank.
scenes.image_prompt: Sam alone at the desk in a bright, empty office, staring at a completely white screen, his hands hovering above the keyboard. Jo's desk beside him is bare: only a small clean square on the wood where her mug used to sit.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Sam leans toward the screen, one finger pressing a single key, the cursor blinking on blank white.

scenes.narration: At dawn, the cliff was quiet. The family was gone.
scenes.image_prompt: The cliff ledge at first light: the nest dented and empty, no fish, no mother, no brother. Orin sits alone in the middle, mid-yawn, one wing stretched, the realization not yet reached his face. The marmot sits at the far end, still.

scenes.narration: He finally dived. The river had been mud for weeks.
scenes.image_prompt: Orin plunges beak-first from the cliff toward the cracked brown riverbed, wings pinned back, eyes huge, with the oak and its three tiny squirrels streaking past on the side of the frame, their mouths already opening in anticipation.
scenes.image_prompt_b: Orin lies face-down in dried mud, only his tail feathers sticking up, a single fish bone beside him, a small puff of dust still settling. The squirrels in the oak have both paws over their mouths.

scenes.narration: Nobody laughed. Not even the squirrels.
scenes.image_prompt: Orin sits alone in the dry riverbed, mud on his face, his huge wings folded. High in the oak, the three squirrels sit side by side in total silence, no acorns, no tails flicking, one slowly lowering his paw from his mouth.

scenes.narration: A fish lay on the ledge. Nobody asked who left it.
scenes.image_prompt: The empty ledge. In the foreground the marmot sits upright beside a single silver fish and is looking straight into the camera, expression unchanged. Behind it in the oak, the three squirrels sit in a row, also looking straight into the camera. Far below, a tiny Orin stands in the riverbed.

youtube.title: The Eagle Who Never Hunted, and the Squirrels Who Kept Count
youtube.description: Orin is a big, sleepy eagle who has eaten 312 fish and caught none. Three squirrels keep count and mock him out loud, until the day the dry season comes and the laughing stops. A short, dry, quietly stinging fable. Subscribe for more tidalfolio stories.
youtube.pinned_comment: Who in your life has been carrying a little more than their share? Be honest.
